steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In September, the Eastern Time zone in the US observes Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. Madrid, Spain, observes Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

The time difference between EDT and CEST is 6 hours (Madrid is 6 hours ahead of ET). 

Adding 6 hours to 5:00 PM (17:00) results in 11:00 PM (23:00) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru, operates on Peru Time (PET), which is 5 hours behind Coordinated Universal Time (UTC-5). Since there is no daylight saving time in Peru, the offset remains constant.

To find your local time, subtract 5 hours from the UTC deadline:
12:00 UTC - 5 hours = 07:00.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST (Central European Summer Time) is UTC+2, while Tokyo (Japan Standard Time) is UTC+9. Since Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST, you add 7 hours to the deadline.

9:00 AM + 7 hours = 16:00 (4:00 PM) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid, we first identify the time zone offsets:
1.  **PDT (Pacific Daylight Time)** is UTC-7.
2.  **Madrid** in October follows Central European Summer Time (**CEST**), which is UTC+2. (Daylight saving in Spain ends on the last Sunday of October, so it will still be in effect on October 11).

The time difference between PDT and CEST is 9 hours (2 - (-7) = 9). 

Adding 9 hours to October 11, 2026, at 11:59 PM (23:59):
*   23:59 + 1 minute = 00:00 on October 12.
*   Adding the remaining 8 hours and 59 minutes results in 08:59 on October 12.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 3, 2026, the Pacific Standard Time (PST) zone is at UTC-8. Since the US Daylight Saving Time transition in 2026 does not occur until March 8, the offset remains -8. Madrid, Spain, will be on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1, as the European Daylight Saving transition does not occur until late March.

Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PST. Adding 9 hours to March 3, 2026, at 11:59 PM (23:59) brings the time to 08:59 AM on the following day.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Central European Time (CET) is UTC+1. Los Angeles, being in the Pacific Time Zone, will be on Pacific Standard Time (PST), which is UTC-8, in February. There is a 9-hour time difference between CET and PST. Subtracting 9 hours from 10:00 AM CET results in 1:00 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Japan Standard Time (JST) is UTC+9, while Lima, Peru, is in Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5. This means JST is 14 hours ahead of your local time.

To find the deadline in Lima:
1. Start with May 5, 2026, at 08:00.
2. Subtract 14 hours.
3. Subtracting 8 hours brings you to 00:00 on May 5.
4. Subtracting the remaining 6 hours brings you to 18:00 on the previous day, May 4.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 28, 2026, the US Pacific Time zone will still be in Daylight Saving Time (PDT, which is UTC-7). In Madrid, Daylight Saving Time (CEST) ends on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026. Therefore, on the date of the deadline, Madrid will have already transitioned to Central European Time (CET, which is UTC+1). 

The time difference between UTC-7 and UTC+1 is 8 hours. Adding 8 hours to 11:59 PM on October 28 results in 7:59 AM on the following day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 30, 2026, the Eastern Time zone in North America will still be in Daylight Saving Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. However, in Spain, Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026), meaning Madrid will have switched to Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1.

The time difference between UTC-4 and UTC+1 is 5 hours. Therefore, 9:00 AM ET plus 5 hours is 2:00 PM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In October 2026, Europe will have transitioned from CEST to CET (UTC+1) on October 25. Meanwhile, New York will still be on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, which is UTC-4) until November 1. 

The difference between CET (UTC+1) and EDT (UTC-4) is 5 hours. Subtracting 5 hours from 18:00 CET results in 13:00.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On November 2, 2026, the United States will be on Pacific Standard Time (PST), which is UTC-8 (Daylight Saving Time ends on November 1, 2026). Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1 (Daylight Saving Time ends on October 25, 2026). Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Pacific Time.

Adding 9 hours to November 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM (23:59) moves the time to 8:59 AM on the following day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In March 2026, the Pacific Time zone will be observing Daylight Saving Time (PDT, which is UTC-7), as the switch occurs on March 8. Madrid, Spain, will still be observing Central European Time (CET, which is UTC+1), as the switch to summer time in Europe does not occur until March 29. Therefore, Madrid is 8 hours ahead of Pacific Time. 

Adding 8 hours to March 20, 2026, at 11:59 PM results in 7:59 AM the following morning.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 25, 2026, Los Angeles will be observing Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7. Since Europe will not have transitioned to Summer Time until March 29, 2026, the time provided (CET) is UTC+1. The time difference between CET (UTC+1) and PDT (UTC-7) is 8 hours. Subtracting 8 hours from 12:00 PM results in 4:00 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In October 2026, both the Eastern Time zone in the US and Madrid, Spain, will be observing Daylight Saving Time. Specifically, the Eastern Time zone will be in EDT (UTC-4) and Madrid will be in CEST (UTC+2). 

Because Madrid is 6 hours ahead of ET (2 - (-4) = 6), 12:00 AM (midnight) at the start of October 12 in the ET zone corresponds to 6:00 AM on the same day in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

"AoE" (Anywhere on Earth) refers to the time zone UTC-12. In Madrid, Spain, on October 9, 2026, you will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

To find your local time, you calculate the difference between UTC-12 and UTC+2, which is 14 hours. Adding 14 hours to October 9, 23:59, results in October 10, 13:59.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In August, both the Pacific Time zone and Madrid are observing Daylight Saving Time. 

1.  **Pacific Time (PT):** In August, this will be Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is **UTC-7**.
2.  **Madrid Time:** In August, Madrid observes Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is **UTC+2**.
3.  **The Offset:** The difference between UTC-7 and UTC+2 is **9 hours** (Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PT).

Adding 9 hours to 12:00 PM (noon) results in 21:00 (9:00 PM) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine your local deadline, we first identify the time zones:
1. **IST (India Standard Time)** is UTC +5:30.
2. **Madrid, Spain**, in November follows **CET (Central European Time)**, which is UTC +1:00.

The time difference between IST and CET is 4 hours and 30 minutes (IST is ahead of Madrid). 

To find your local time, we subtract 4 hours and 30 minutes from 11:59 PM (23:59):
- 23:59 - 4 hours = 19:59
- 19:59 - 30 minutes = 19:29

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."

Nepal is in the Nepal Standard Time zone (UTC+5:45), while Lima, Peru, is in the Peru Time zone (UTC-5). This creates a time difference of 10 hours and 45 minutes. To find your local time, subtract 10 hours and 45 minutes from 5:00 PM (17:00) on April 2, 2026.

17:00 - 10 hours = 07:00
07:00 - 45 minutes = 06:15

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In October 2026, Adelaide, Australia, will be observing Australian Central Daylight Time (ACDT), which is UTC+10:30 (daylight saving starts on October 4, 2026). Madrid, Spain, will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2. 

The time difference is 8 hours and 30 minutes. Subtracting this from 10:00 AM Adelaide time results in 01:30 AM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 3, 2026, Sydney will be using Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST), which is UTC+10, because Daylight Saving Time in Australia does not begin until the first Sunday of October (October 4, 2026). Madrid will be using Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2. Since Sydney is 8 hours ahead of Madrid, you subtract 8 hours from 6:00 PM (18:00).

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
